questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
The electric field associated with an electromagnetic wave travelling in vacuum is given by $E_0 \sin(3y + 4z + \omega t)\,\hat{i}$, where $\omega$ is the angular frequency. All quantities are in SI units. The correct statement(s) about this wave is/are:
[Given: speed of light in vacuum $c = 3 \times 10^8$ ms$^{-1}$.]
options: The wave is travelling in $-\dfrac{1}{5}(3\hat{j} + 4\hat{k})$ direction.
The magnitude of the wave vector is $0.5$ m$^{-1}$.
The value of $\omega$ is $1.5 \times 10^9$ rad s$^{-1}$.
The magnetic field associated with this wave is given by $\dfrac{E_0}{c}\sin(3y + 4z + \omega t)(4\hat{j} - 3\hat{k})$.
questions.solution:
The given electric field is $\vec{E} = E_0 \sin(3y + 4z + \omega t)\,\hat{i}$.

Comparing the phase $\phi = 3y + 4z + \omega t$ with the standard wave equation phase $\vec{k} \cdot \vec{r} - \omega t$, we can rewrite it as $-(-3y - 4z - \omega t)$.

Thus, the wave vector is $\vec{k} = -3\hat{j} - 4\hat{k}$.

The direction of wave propagation is given by the unit vector $\hat{n}$:

$\hat{n} = \dfrac{\vec{k}}{|\vec{k}|} = \dfrac{-3\hat{j} - 4\hat{k}}{\sqrt{(-3)^2 + (-4)^2}} = -\dfrac{1}{5}(3\hat{j} + 4\hat{k})$

The magnitude of the wave vector is $|\vec{k}| = 5$ m$^{-1}$.

The angular frequency $\omega$ is:

$\omega = c|\vec{k}| = (3 \times 10^8) \times 5 = 1.5 \times 10^9$ rad s$^{-1}$

The magnetic field $\vec{B}$ is given by:

$\vec{B} = \dfrac{1}{c}(\hat{n} \times \vec{E}) = \dfrac{1}{c} \left[ -\dfrac{1}{5}(3\hat{j} + 4\hat{k}) \right] \times [E_0 \sin(3y + 4z + \omega t)\,\hat{i}]$

$\vec{B} = -\dfrac{E_0}{5c} \sin(3y + 4z + \omega t) [3(\hat{j} \times \hat{i}) + 4(\hat{k} \times \hat{i})]$

$\vec{B} = -\dfrac{E_0}{5c} \sin(3y + 4z + \omega t) (-3\hat{k} + 4\hat{j}) = \dfrac{E_0}{5c} \sin(3y + 4z + \omega t) (-4\hat{j} + 3\hat{k})$

Answer: The wave is travelling in $-\dfrac{1}{5}(3\hat{j} + 4\hat{k})$ direction.; The value of $\omega$ is $1.5 \times 10^9$ rad s$^{-1}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A cube of unit volume contains $35 \times 10^7$ photons of frequency $10^{15} \mathrm{~Hz}$. If the energy of all the photons is viewed as the average energy being contained in the electromagnetic waves within the same volume, then the amplitude of the magnetic field is $\alpha \times 10^{-9} \mathrm{~T}$. Taking permeability of free space $\mu_0=4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \mathrm{Tm} / \mathrm{A}$, Planck's constant $h=6 \times 10^{-34} \mathrm{Js}$ and $\pi=\frac{22}{7}$, the value of $\alpha$ is_______
questions.solution:
Total energy in cube $=35 \times 10^7 \times \mathrm{hf}$
$\begin{aligned} & =35 \times 10^7 \times 6 \times 10^{-34} \times 10^{15} \\ & =2.1 \times 10^{-10} \mathrm{~J}\end{aligned}$
Total energy of EM waves $=\frac{B_0^2}{2 \mu_0} \times$ volume
$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{B}_0^2=\frac{2.1 \times 10^{-10} \times 8 \pi \times 10^{-7}}{1^3} \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{~B}_0=22.98 \times 10^{-9} \mathrm{~T}\end{aligned}$
Ans. 22.98

questions.q: A metal target with atomic number $Z=46$ is bombarded with a high energy electron beam. The emission of X-rays from the target is analyzed. The ratio $r$ of the wavelengths of the $K_\alpha$-line and the cut-off is found to be $r=2$. If the same electron beam bombards another metal target with $Z=41$, the value of $r$ will be
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \frac{1}{\lambda_\alpha}=\frac{3}{4} R(Z-1)^2 p \\ & \lambda_{\text{cut }}=\frac{h c}{e V} \\ & \Rightarrow \text{ Ratio } \propto \frac{1}{(Z-1)^2} \text{$ for $same beam } \\ & \frac{Z}{x}=\frac{40^2}{45^2} \\ & \Rightarrow x=\frac{45^2}{40^2} .2 \approx 2.53 \end{aligned}\)$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
The electric field associated with an electromagnetic wave propagating in a dielectric medium is given by $\overset{\to}{E} = 30\left(2\overset{∧}{x} + \overset{∧}{y}\right)sin\left[2\pi\left(5 \times {10}^{14}t - \dfrac{{10}^{7}}{3}z\right)\right]V{m}^{- 1}$. Which of the following option(s) is(are) correct?

[Given: The speed of light in vacuum, $c = 3 \times {10}^{8}m{s}^{– 1}$]
options: The wave is polarized in the $xy$-plane with polarization angle ${30}^{o}$ with respect to the $x$-axis
The refractive index of the medium is $2$
questions.solution:
Speed of light in medium is $v = \dfrac{\omega}{k}$

$⇒ v = \dfrac{2\pi\left(5 \times {10}^{14}\right)}{2\pi \times \dfrac{{10}^{7}}{3}}$

$⇒ v = 1 . 5 \times {10}^{8}m{s}^{- 1}$

Therefore, refractive index $\mu = \dfrac{c}{v} = \dfrac{3 \times {10}^{8}}{1 . 5 \times {10}^{8}} = 2$

$⇒ \mu = 2$

Given $\overset{\to}{E} = 30\left(2\overset{∧}{x} + \overset{∧}{y}\right)sin\left(2\pi\left(5 \times {10}^{14}t - \dfrac{{10}^{7}}{3}z\right)\right)V{m}^{- 1}$

The wave is polarised in $xy -$plane with polarisation angle $\tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)$ with respect to $x -$axis.

Amplitude of magnetic field, ${B}_{0} = \dfrac{{E}_{0}}{V} = \dfrac{30\sqrt{{2}^{2} + {1}^{2}}}{1 . 5 \times {10}^{8}} = \dfrac{30\sqrt{5}}{1 . 5 \times {10}^{8}}$

Now, direction of $\overset{\to}{B}$ is $\left(\overset{\to}{v} \times \overset{\to}{E}\right)$

$= \overset{∧}{k} \times \dfrac{\left(2\overset{∧}{i} + \overset{∧}{j}\right)}{\sqrt{5}}$

$= \left(\dfrac{- \overset{∧}{i} + 2\overset{∧}{j}}{\sqrt{5}}\right)$.

$\overset{\to}{B} = \left(\dfrac{- \overset{∧}{i} + 2\overset{∧}{j}}{\sqrt{5}}\right) \times \dfrac{30\sqrt{5}}{1 . 5 \times {10}^{8}}sin\left[2\pi\left(5 \times {10}^{14}t - \dfrac{{10}^{7}}{3}z\right)\right]Wb{m}^{- 2} = \left(- \overset{∧}{i} + 2\overset{∧}{j}\right) \times 2 \times {10}^{- 7}sin\left[2\pi\left(5 \times {10}^{14}t - \dfrac{{10}^{7}}{3}z\right)\right]Wb{m}^{- 2}$

Hence,

${B}_{x} = - 2 \times {10}^{- 7}sin\left[2\pi\left(5 \times {10}^{14}t - \dfrac{{10}^{7}}{3}z\right)\right]Wb{m}^{- 2}$

and ${B}_{y} = 4 \times {10}^{- 7}sin\left[2\pi\left(5 \times {10}^{14}t - \dfrac{{10}^{7}}{3}z\right)\right]Wb{m}^{- 2}$

questions.q: In an $X$-ray tube, electrons emitted from a filament (cathode) carrying current $I$ hit a target (anode) at a distance $d$ from the cathode. The target is kept at a potential $V$ higher than the cathode resulting in emission of continuous and characteristic X-rays. If the filament current $I$ is decreased to $\dfrac{I}{2},$ the potential difference $V$ is increased to $2V,$ and the separation distance $d$ is reduced to $\dfrac{d}{2},$ then
options: the cut-off wavelength will reduce to half, and the wavelengths of the characteristic X-rays will remain the same
the cut-off wavelength as well as the wavelengths of the characteristic X-rays will remain the same
the cut-off wavelength will reduce to half, and the intensities of all the X-rays will decrease
the cut-off wavelength will become two times larger, and the intensity of all the X-rays will decrease
questions.solution:
Cut off wavelength ${\lambda}_{C} ∝ \dfrac{1}{V}$

So, cut-off wavelength becomes half.

Characteristic x-ray depends on target atomic number, so it remains same.

On decreasing filament current number of electron decrease, so intensity of $X$ -ray decreases.

questions.q: A fission reaction is given by $U 92236 \to Xe 54140 + Sr 3894 + x + y$ , where $x$ and $y$ are two particles. Considering $U 92236$ to be at rest, the kinetic energies of the products are denoted by ${K}_{Xe}, {K}_{Sr}, {K}_{x} ( 2MeV )$ and ${K}_{y}\left(2MeV\right)$ , respectively. Let the binding energies per nucleon of $U 92236 , Xe 54140$ and $Sr 3894$ be 7.5 MeV, 8.5 MeV, and 8.5 MeV respectively. Considering different conservation laws, the correct option(s) is (are)
questions.solution:
$\begin{array}{ll}U \to Xe + Sr + & x & + \\ 2\end{array}\begin{array}{ll}y \\ 2\end{array}$
$Q = 4 + {K}_{Xe} + {K}_{Sr}$ ...(i)
$- Q = {E}_{B} = 236 \times 7.5 - 140 \times 8.5 - 94 \times 8.5$
$∴ Q = 219$ ...(ii)
$∴ {K}_{Xe} + {K}_{Sr} = 215MeV$
Since, both $x$ & $y$ have same KE
$∴$ both particles should have same mass & lighter body will have higher KE.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Which one of the following statement is WRONG in the context of X-rays generated from X-ray tube?
options:
Wavelength of characteristic X-rays decreases when the atomic number of the target increases

Cut-off wavelength of the continuous X-rays depends on the atomic number of the target

Intensity of the characteristics X-rays depends on the electrical power given to the X-ray tube

Cut-off wavelength of the continuous X-rays depends on the energy of the electrons in the X-ray tube
questions.solution: Cut-off wavelength depends on the applied voltage not on the atomic number of the target. Characteristic wavelengths depend on the atomic number of target.
questions.question: Which one of the following statement is WRONG in the context of X-rays generated from X-ray tube?
questions.explanation: Cut-off wavelength depends on the applied voltage not on the atomic number of the target. Characteristic wavelengths depend on the atomic number of target.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
Statement I If the accelerating potential in an X-ray tube is increased, the wavelengths of the characteristic $X$-rays do not change.
Statement II When an electron beam strikes the target in an X-ray tube, part of the kinetic energy is converted into X-ray energy.
options:
Statement I is true, Statement II is true; Statement II is a correct explanation for Statement I

Statement I is true, Statement II is true; Statement II is NOT a correct explanation for Statement I

Statement I is true, Statement II is false

Statement I is false, Statement II is true
questions.solution:
Cut-off wavelength depends on the accelerating voltage, not the characteristic $\mathrm{X}$-rays. Further approximately $2 \%$ kinetic energy of the electrons is utilised in producing X-rays. Rest $98 \%$ is lost in heat.
$\therefore$ Option (b) is correct.
